steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Official statistics: recorded by the police and published by the Home Office. They show that working-class people, men, young people and some ethnic minorities are over-represented. However, official statistics have major limitations: the 'dark figure of crime' (unreported and unrecorded crime) means they significantly underestimate true crime rates. | Key Fact: The dark figure of crime: only about 40% of crime is reported to the police. Reasons: too trivial, police can't do anything, fear of retaliation, embarrassment. Of reported crime, only about 30% is recorded. The real crime rate is much higher than official statistics suggest. | Key Fact: Self-report studies: anonymous surveys asking people what crimes they have committed.
